lines: # Solutions Partner for Modern Work
Appropriate roles: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner admin
A Solutions Partner for Modern work demonstrates a broad capability to help customers boost their productivity and make the shift to hybrid work using Microsoft 365.

To earn this designation, your partner capability score must meet the qualification requirements for this area. You need a minimum of 70 points out of a possible 100 to attain a solutions partner designation.
The score is measured in three categories - partner performance, skilling, and customer success. Your partner capability score calculates from data that is already recorded in Partner Center.
You must attain at least one point in each of the following individual metrics and at least 70 total points.
- Performance - Net customer adds
- Skilling - Intermediate certifications
- Skilling - Advanced certifications
- Customer success - Usage growth
- Customer success - Deployments
You can track your progress towards attaining the Solutions Partner for Modern work designation in Partner Center.
## Start here
- Sign in to Partner Center and select Membership > Solutions Partner > Overview. You need the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner admin role to view the Membership workspace.
- Open the Modern Work details and review your Enterprise and SMB scores. Check all five individual metrics, not just the total score.
- Review the eligible customer associations, workloads, and paid-seat requirements for each metric in this article.
- Link your Microsoft Learn profile and Skilling Hub account so that eligible learning achievements can contribute to your organization's skilling score.
- If a customer or score is missing, follow Troubleshoot missing customers and scores before creating a support request.
- When you're qualified, review enrollment and renewal status, purchase the designation, and review the benefits.
## Two attainment paths: Enterprise and small and medium business

Microsoft offers two distinct paths for achieving the Solutions Partner for Modern Work designation: the Enterprise path and the Small and Medium Business (SMB) path, each with its own set of criteria. This dual-path approach lets partners select the path that aligns with their customer focus, whether it be SMB or Enterprise customers.

Microsoft evaluates partners on both paths and selects the highest score from either path. Microsoft selects the highest score at the solution area level, rather than at the individual metric level, to determine qualification. This process helps to ensure that partners can use the path that best suits their business strategy.
You can't combine the best individual metric scores from the Enterprise and SMB paths to create a qualifying score.
## Performance category
The Performance category is a measure of your organization's ability to increase the customer base using Microsoft products for Modern work and productivity.
There's one metric in the Performance category:
- Net customer adds metric
The Net customer adds Enterprise path criteria and SMB path criteria are different. The details are explained in the following sections.
### Performance: Net customer adds metric

The Net customer adds metric for Modern Work is the change in the number of qualifying customer tenants over the trailing 12-month period. A customer tenant must meet the applicable workload, paid-seat, and association requirements to contribute to the count.
Scoring:
Enterprise track: Each net new customer added contributes to four points, for up to a maximum of 20 points, from five customers.
SMB track: Each net new customer added contributes two points, for up to a maximum of 20 points, from 10 customers.
Calculation:
Net customer adds = [Total qualifying current customer tenants] - [Total qualifying customers tenants 12 months ago]

Compare the latest available reporting month with the corresponding month 12 months earlier, not with the previous month. Adding customers doesn't necessarily increase the net value: customers that no longer qualify can offset new qualifying customers.
The following illustrative examples show the raw Net customer adds value, not the points awarded:
Current qualifying tenants | Qualifying tenants in the corresponding month last year | Net customer adds
For a positive net value of two qualifying customers, the SMB scoring rate produces four points and the Enterprise scoring rate produces eight points, subject to the 20-point maximum.
Eligible customer tenants:
Enterprise track: Each customer tenant that has at least one workload with paid licenses greater than 300 is counted as an eligible tenant.

SMB Track: Each customer tenant that has least one workload with paid licenses between 11 to 300 is counted as an eligible tenant. A customer tenant promoted to Enterprise remains eligible for SMB if it was classified as SMB in the previous year

The paid-seat requirement applies to at least one eligible workload within a customer tenant. Don't add unrelated workloads or seats from different customer tenants together to meet that requirement. A product or subscription name alone doesn't establish metric eligibility; check the eligible workload and its paid seats.
Note
The same tenant can participate in both the Enterprise and SMB tracks.
Eligible workloads:
The eligible workloads for both tracks include:
- Exchange Online
- Intune
- M365 Copilot
- Microsoft 365 Apps
- Microsoft Entra ID P1
- SharePoint Online
- Teams
- Teams Apps
- Teams for Frontline Workers
- Teams Meetings
- Teams Phone
- Teams Phone calling
- Teams Phone Enabled Users
- Teams Rooms Monthly Active Devices
- Viva Connections
- Viva Engage
- Viva Goals
- Viva Insights
- Viva Learning
- Viva Topics
- Windows 365
Eligible association types:
Track | Eligible association types
Enterprise | Claiming Partner of Record (CPOR), Digital Partner of Record (DPOR)
SMB | CPOR, Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) Tier 1 or Tier 2

Delegated administrative privileges (DAP) or granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP) provide administrative access. That access alone isn't one of the eligible associations listed in this table. A customer you can administer must still have an eligible association for the track and metric.

For CPOR, verify the customer, workload, partner location, and association status in Incentives > Customer claims. An approved association doesn't mean the same data is already available in the designation score. See Create customer associations with the Claiming Partner of Record model and Data freshness.

A customer can have multiple partners, but a Modern Work and Security Usage workload can be associated with only one partner through the CPOR claiming process. If a claim is rejected, review the reason and resolve the claim issue through the relevant Incentives support workflow rather than treating the rejected claim as a qualifying association.
Return to top
## Skilling category
The skilling category measures your organization's skills and capabilities by using the number of persons who have an eligible certification.
Important

Retired certifications: If an eligible certification is earned before its retirement date, the certified individual continues to receive credit for that certification for one year after the certification's retirement date. During this period, the certification continues to count toward the applicable skilling requirements for Solutions Partner designations and Specializations.
- Each person with an eligible certification can contribute to the applicable skilling metric. Multiple eligible credentials held by that person don't increase their count within the same metric.
- There are two attainment paths: Small and medium business and Enterprise.
- There are two metrics in this Skilling category : Intermediate and Advanced

- To fulfill the requirement to have more than zero points in every metric, your organization must have at least one qualifying person with an intermediate certification, and the same person or a different person with an advanced certification.
Certified persons required to earn the maximum of 25 points in the Skilling category:
Path | Intermediate certifications (10 points max) | Advanced certifications (15 points max)
Enterprise | Four certified persons | Two certified persons
Small & Medium Business | Two certified persons | One certified person
Eligible Microsoft 365 certifications:
The eligible Microsoft 365 certifications include:
- Intermediate metric
- Microsoft 365 Fundamentals
- Microsoft 365 Certified: Teams Administrator Associate
- Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate
- Microsoft 365 Certified: Collaboration Communications Systems Engineer Associate
- Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate (previously known as Microsoft 365 Certified: Modern Desktop Administrator Associate)
- Microsoft 365 Certified: Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals
- Advanced metric
- Microsoft 365 Certified: Microsoft 365 and AI Services Administrator Associate
- Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert (previously Enterprise Administrator Expert)
- Teams Meetings and Meeting Rooms Technical Assessment
Retirement and legacy recognition:
Credential or assessment | Metric | Retirement date | Published recognition through
Microsoft 365 Fundamentals | Intermediate | March 31, 2026 | March 31, 2027
Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert | Advanced | November 30, 2026 | November 30, 2027
Teams Meetings and Meeting Rooms Technical Assessment | Advanced | June 15, 2026 | June 15, 2027

Apply the retirement-credit guidance to achievements earned before retirement. A retired credential's presence in this list doesn't mean that a new learner can still complete it. Check the credential or assessment's published availability when planning new learning.
Administrator Expert earned before November 30, 2026 remains eligible for partner capability score points through November 30, 2027.

An announced successor isn't automatically eligible for the same designation metric or a related specialization. Use this article's eligible list and the applicable specialization requirements. If the published program information doesn't establish a future replacement mapping, request clarification rather than inferring it from an exam code or certification title.
Important considerations:
- Each certified individual is counted once for this metric, even if the certified individual completes multiple certifications.
- Intermediate certifications can be earned by the same individual, or different individuals, than the Advanced certifications.

- Some of these certifications might have prerequisites listed on the certification website (select the individual certification links). Those prerequisites must be addressed in order for a person to complete certification.
### Why isn't my employee counted in skilling?
Check these requirements separately:

- Awarded achievement: Verify the full credential or explicitly eligible assessment, not only a course or exam pass. For example, passing MS-102 alone doesn't establish that Administrator Expert is awarded; review the credential's current prerequisites.
- Correct profile and organization: Confirm that the employee linked the profile holding the achievement to the intended Partner Center organization.
- Source data and timing: Check association and report evidence and the synchronization guidance in the Learn profile linking FAQs.
- Metric eligibility and dates: Match the achievement to Intermediate or Advanced and review the retirement and recognition dates above.

- Unique individuals: Count each person once within the metric. The same person can contribute to both metrics when they hold eligible credentials for each, but two Advanced credentials held by that person don't count as two Advanced-certified people.

Skilling is only part of qualification. For example, a total of 85 points with zero Advanced Certification points doesn't meet the requirement to earn points in every required metric. Review qualification and renewal status separately.

If the counts still differ, reconcile the contributing learners with the score. Completing a course, linking a platform account, or reaching the Skilling maximum doesn't by itself meet every requirement for the designation.
## Customer success category
The customer success category measures your ability to enable growth in using Microsoft products or expanding Microsoft's services and workloads that customers use.
There are two metrics in the Customer success category:
- Usage growth metric
- Deployments metric
### Customer success: Usage growth metric

This customer success metric measures your ability to grow the use and consumption of our qualifying products. You earn points for this metric based on the growth exhibited in the Usage growth across all your eligible customer tenants and workloads.
Calculation:
Usage growth = [Eligible Active users last month] - [Eligible Active users same month last year]
Eligible Active users:
The number of active users across all eligible customer tenants from all eligible workloads for specific partner association types.
Eligible customer tenants:
Enterprise track: Each customer tenant that has at least one workload with paid licenses greater than 300 is counted to be an eligible Tenant for the Enterprise track.

SMB track: Each customer tenant that has at least one workload with paid licenses between 11 to 300 is counted to be an eligible Tenant for the SMB track. A customer tenant promoted to Enterprise remains eligible for SMB if it was classified as SMB in the previous year.
Eligible workloads:
The eligible workloads for both tracks include:
- Exchange Online
- Intune
- M365 Copilot
- Microsoft 365 Apps
- Microsoft Entra ID P1
- SharePoint Online
- Teams
- Teams Apps
- Teams for Frontline Workers
- Teams Meetings
- Teams Phone
- Teams Phone calling
- Teams Phone Enabled Users
- Teams Premium
- Teams Rooms Monthly Active Devices
- Viva Connections
- Viva Engage
- Viva Goals
- Viva Insights
- Viva Learning
- Viva Topics
- Windows 365
Eligible associations:
Enterprise Track: Claiming Partner of Record (CPOR) & Digital Partner of Record (DPOR) are valid association types
SMB Track: Claiming Partner of Record (CPOR) &CSP (Tier 1 & Tier 2) are valid association types
Note
You can only receive points for usage growth from the time you claim or associate with a customer. You don't receive credit for Usage growth that existed before your association.
Thresholds to earn maximum points - Enterprise track:

In the Enterprise eligibility path, you get points for usage growth based on the association type. Two options are created: CPOR and DPOR. Each option has different thresholds. You get different points for each option based on your performance against those thresholds. Qualifying points for usage growth is the higher of the points obtained from the two options, CPOR and DPOR.
Option | Threshold for maximum points
CPOR | 1,000 Usage growth
DPOR | 4,000 Usage growth
Scoring example:
Partial scoring is applied for any Usage growth, up to a maximum of 30 points, obtained from 1,000 Usage growth (for CPOR) OR 4,000 Usage growth (for DPOR), whichever is higher.
For example, if you have 2,000 Usage growth from DPOR associations over the past 12 months and 1,500 Usage growth from CPOR associations, the scoring for the Usage growth metric is:
DPOR based growth = 2,000 Usage growth DPOR based points = (actual growth / threshold growth level) * max points = 2,000/4,000 * 30 = 15
CPOR based growth = 1,500 Usage growth CPOR based points = (actual growth / threshold growth level) * max points = 1,500/1,000 * 30 = 45
Usage growth net score = 30 ~ higher of 15 and 45 from above, for up to a maximum of 30
Thresholds to earn maximum points - SMB track:

In the SMB eligibility path, you earn points for Usage growth based on the association type. Two options are created: CPOR and CSP. Each option has different thresholds. You get different points for each option based on your performance against those thresholds. Qualifying points for Usage growth is the higher of the points obtained from the two options, CPOR and CSP.
Option | Threshold for max points
CPOR | 500 monthly active users (MAU)
CSP | 2,000 MAU
Scoring example:
Partial scoring is applied for any Usage growth, up to a maximum of 30 points, obtained from 500 Usage growth (CPOR) or 2,000 Usage growth (CSP), whichever is highest.
For example, if you have 1,000 Usage growth from CSP associations over the past 12 months and 1,000 Usage growth from CPOR associations, scoring is decided for usage growth metric as follows:
CSP based growth = 1,000 Usage growth CSP based points = (actual growth / threshold growth level) * max points = 1,000/2,000 * 30 = 15
CPOR based growth = 1,000 Usage growth CPOR based points = (actual growth / threshold growth level) * max points = 1,000/500 * 30 = 60
Usage growth score = 30 ~ higher of 15 and 60 from above, for up to a maximum of 30
Note

Targets differ for different association types for both SMB and Enterprise. You can earn points only for one association type per metric. If you have more than one association type, we award points based on the one that earns the most points.
### Customer success: Deployments metric

This metric in the customer success category measures your ability to grow the deployments of our Microsoft 365 services. You earn points for this metric based on the growth in deployments of eligible workloads with a minimum monthly usage level.
Calculation:
Deployments = (Eligible deployments last month) - (Eligible deployments same month last year)
The preceding calculation excludes deployments that were claimed or associated within the last 12 months and were already greater than 40% at the time of claim or association.
Eligible Deployments:
Eligible deployments are unique eligible customer tenants that meet the 40% monthly active usage requirement for paid licenses in eligible workloads, for the applicable partner association type.

Paid available units (PAU) represent paid seats, and monthly active users (MAU) represent active usage. For an illustrative workload with 50 eligible paid seats and 20 monthly active users, the usage ratio is 20 / 50 * 100 = 40%. Meeting that usage ratio is only one check: the tenant must also meet the track, workload, association, and deployment calculation requirements.

Hours spent working with a customer or purchasing licenses don't replace the active-usage requirement. A tenant that meets the paid-seat criteria for Net customer adds doesn't automatically contribute to Deployments.
Eligible customer tenants:
Enterprise track: Each customer tenant having at least one workload with paid licenses greater than 300 is counted to be an eligible Tenant for Enterprise track.

SMB track: Each customer tenant having at least one workload with paid licenses between 11 to 300 is counted to be an eligible Tenant for SMB track. A customer tenant promoted to Enterprise remains eligible for SMB if it was classified as SMB in the previous year
Eligible workloads:
The eligible workloads for both tracks include:
- Exchange Online
- Intune
- M365 Copilot
- Microsoft 365 Apps
- Microsoft Entra ID P1
- SharePoint Online
- Teams
- Teams Apps
- Teams for Frontline Workers
- Teams Meetings
- Teams Phone Teams Phone calling
- Teams Phone Enabled Users
- Teams Premium
- Teams Rooms Monthly Active Devices
- Viva Connections
- Viva Engage
- Viva Goals
- Viva Insights
- Viva Learning
- Viva Topics
- Windows 365
Eligible associations:
Enterprise Track: The Claiming Partner of Record (CPOR) & Digital Partner of Record (DPOR) are valid association types.
SMB Track: The Claiming Partner of Record (CPOR) &CSP (Tier 1 & Tier 2) are valid association types.
Threshold for maximum points - Enterprise track:

In the Enterprise eligibility path, you get points for deployments based on the association type. Two options are created: CPOR and DPOR. Each option has different thresholds. Based on your performance against those thresholds, you get different points for each option. Qualifying points for deployments is the higher of the points obtained from the two options, CPOR and DPOR.
Option | Threshold for maximum points
CPOR | Five net new deployments
DPOR | 10 net new deployments
Scoring example:
- Each new qualifying CPOR deployment gets five points OR each new qualifying DPOR deployment gets 2.5 points, whichever aggregates to higher points, for up to a maximum of 25 points.
For example, if you have four net new deployments from DPOR associations over the past 12 months and 3 from CPOR associations, the scoring is decided for deployments metric as follows:
DPOR based deployments = 4 DPOR based points = (actual deployments / threshold deployments level) * max points = 4/10 * 25 = 10 points
CPOR based deployments = 3 CPOR based points = (actual deployments / threshold deployments level) * max points = 3/5 * 25 = 15 points
**Deployments net score = 15** ~ higher of 15 and 10 from above, for up to a maximum of 25
Threshold for maximum points - SMB track:

In the SMB eligibility path, you get points for deployments based on the association type. Two options are created: CPOR and CSP. Each option has different thresholds. You get different points for each option based on your performance against those thresholds. Qualifying points for deployments is the higher of the points obtained from the two options, CPOR and CSP.
Option | Threshold for max points
CPOR | Five net new deployments
CSP | 10 net new deployments
Scoring example:
- Each new qualifying CPOR deployment gets five points OR each new qualifying CSP deployment gets 2.5 points, whichever aggregates to higher points, for up to a maximum of 25 points.
For example, if you have four net-new deployments from CSP associations over the past 12 months and 3 from CPOR associations, the scoring is decided for deployments metric as follows:
CSP based deployments = 4 CSP based points = (actual deployments / threshold deployments level) * max points = 4/10 * 25 = 10 points
CPOR based deployments = 3 CPOR based points = (actual deployments / threshold deployments level) * max points = 3/5 * 25 = 15 points
Deployments net score = 15 ~ higher of 15 and 10 from above, for up to a maximum of 25
Note
Targets differ for different association types for both SMB and Enterprise, and you can only earn points for one association type per metric.
If you have more than one association type, we award points based on the one that earns the most points.
Don't add the CPOR and CSP or DPOR points together. This association-level comparison for an individual metric is different from selecting the highest overall Enterprise or SMB pathway score.
## Data freshness

Performance and Customer Success subcategories typically refresh by the 20th of every month. There might also be minor data refreshes throughout the month. Skilling subcategories typically refresh within 10 days after certification completes. For profile-linking timing, see Link your Microsoft Learn profile and Skilling Hub account.
Customer association, source-data availability, and score refresh are separate steps:
- The customer association is established or the relevant claim is approved.
- The association and eligible workload data become available in the source reports.
- The designation metrics reflect the data available for the reporting period when they refresh.

Check the reporting month available in Partner Center before comparing the score with a recently added customer. If the latest report covers a period before the association became effective, the report doesn't yet establish whether that new association will contribute to a later score.

The typical refresh schedule isn't a guarantee that every recently approved association appears on a particular date. If Partner Center displays a processing or delay notice, review the notice and the reporting month before treating an unchanged score as an eligibility failure.
Return to top
## Troubleshoot missing customers and scores
Use these checks to distinguish an eligibility issue from missing or delayed data.
Check | What to review | Next action
Track and metric | Enterprise or SMB; Net customer adds, Usage growth, or Deployments | Apply the requirements for that track and metric, not another designation's rules.
Association | CPOR/DPOR for Enterprise or CPOR/CSP for SMB | Verify an eligible association. DAP/GDAP access alone doesn't establish eligibility.
Workload and paid seats | Eligible workload and paid seats for the customer tenant | Review the workload criteria; don't infer eligibility from a product name or combine unrelated seat counts.
Claim or relationship status | Correct customer, workload, partner location, and active/approved association | Resolve setup or rejected-claim issues before expecting that association to contribute.
Reporting period | Latest reporting month and any processing/delay notice | Compare the association date with the period available; review Data freshness.
Comparison baseline | Current qualifying count and the corresponding month 12 months earlier | Customers that no longer qualify can offset newly qualifying customers.
### Download and reconcile the supporting data
- Open Membership > Solutions Partner > Overview, select Modern Work, and open the relevant metric details. Download the supporting data where available.
- Review the Customer Eligibility report for the affected customer and metric. Confirm the track, filters, and whether the reported conditions are met.
- For usage investigation, use the Download Reports hub in Insights and the Microsoft 365 usage report data definitions.
- Compare the same metric, association type, workload, track, and corresponding reporting months. Review these fields where available:
Field | Why it matters
Month | Identifies the reporting period, which can differ from the date you view the portal.
CustomerTenantId and WorkloadName | Identify the customer tenant and workload being investigated.
PaidAvailableUnits and MonthlyActiveUsers | Help check paid-seat and active-usage requirements.
PartnerAttributionType | Shows the recorded relationship; not every attribution in a general usage report is eligible for designation points.
PGAPartnerID and PartnerID | Help verify global and location account context.
IsDuplicateRowForPGA | Identifies duplicate attribution rows in the general usage report; don't count every row as a distinct qualifying customer.

The partner global account and partner location accounts serve different purposes. CSP and incentives associations use location accounts. Verify that the association belongs to the organization whose qualification you're reviewing.

A blank download isn't by itself proof that the customer count is zero. Check your role, filters, reporting period, and eligible associations. The general Microsoft 365 usage report helps investigate the underlying data, but its presence or row count alone doesn't establish a customer's designation eligibility.
### Check deployment and usage-growth expectations
If a customer contributes to one metric but not another, review the requirements separately:
- Net customer adds compares qualifying customer tenants with the corresponding month last year.
- Usage growth compares eligible active users with the corresponding month last year. Usage before your association doesn't contribute to your usage growth.

- Deployments applies the usage requirement, year-over-year calculation, and exclusion described in Deployments metric. A workload already above the usage threshold when associated can be excluded by that calculation.
Use the association-specific scoring examples in this article. Don't combine CPOR and CSP/DPOR scores or the best metrics from different pathways.
### Check renewal status separately from current qualification
Being qualified today doesn't mean your renewal payment window is open. Review enrollment, qualification history, the qualification eligibility window, and renewal status in Partner Capability Score.

If Buy Now or Renew Now is disabled, follow Troubleshoot membership purchase. Before renewal, check all required metrics and the available reporting month rather than assuming a recent customer association has already changed your score.
### Contact the right support team

If the checks don't explain the difference, follow Get help and contact support. Include the track, metric, reporting month, expected result, association status/date, relevant report extracts, and any processing notice. Include your renewal deadline if the issue is time-sensitive.

Use Membership for designation qualification or renewal questions, Insights for report-data questions, and Incentives for CPOR claim or incentive-payment questions. For CSP setup or Microsoft 365 administration, use the relevant workflow in Which support portal should I use?.

lines: # Introduction to Solutions Partner designations
Appropriate roles: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner admin
## Silver or gold membership
Microsoft no longer offers Silver and gold memberships. Partners should stop using references to Silver and gold membership in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program.
## Overview

The Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program offers three Solutions Partner designation badges and six Solutions Partner designation pathways. Partners can earn designation badges and incremental benefits to stand out from the competition and increase their customer reach.
- Solutions Partner for Cloud & AI Platforms
- Data and AI (Azure) pathway
- Digital and App Innovation (Azure) pathway
- Infrastructure (Azure) pathway
- Solutions Partner for Security
- Security pathway
- Solutions Partner for AI Business Solutions
- Business Applications pathway
- Modern Work pathway
## Solutions Partner designation badges

Each Solutions Partner designation pathway contributes to one of three Solutions Partner designation badges. These badges align to Microsoft's commercial solution areas and let you showcase your capabilities within the broader solution area, while you retain full visibility into your individual designation pathway progress and score.

The way you qualify, enroll, earn benefits, and are scored for each designation is unchanged. You continue to see and work with the six individual designations in Partner Center; the badge is an external representation that rolls up the designations you earned.
Solutions Partner designation pathway | Solutions Partner designation badge
Data & AI (Azure) | Solutions Partner for Cloud & AI Platforms
Infrastructure (Azure) | Solutions Partner for Cloud & AI Platforms
Digital & App Innovation (Azure) | Solutions Partner for Cloud & AI Platforms
Modern Work | Solutions Partner for AI Business Solutions
Business Applications | Solutions Partner for AI Business Solutions
Security | Solutions Partner for Security

Qualifying for any designation pathway that maps to a badge earns you that badge. Your individual designation pathway names, capability scores, and progress remain unchanged and visible in Partner Center.
## Qualify for Solutions Partner designations

Eligibility for Solutions Partner designations is based on the partner capability score achieved by your organization. A partner capability score is a composite score that quantifies performance across three categories - Performance, Skilling, and Customer success. This score is calculated through measurements based on information already captured in Partner Center. Learn more about how this score is calculated.
Partners with the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner admin role can track progress toward attaining any Solutions Partner designation from the Solutions Partner dashboard.
## Purchase the Solutions Partner designations

Once you're qualified in one or more designation pathways, your status changes to qualified. You can then proceed with payment to enroll in the Solutions Partner designation offer. Learn more about how to make a payment.
## Renew the Solutions Partner designations

After you purchase the Solutions Partner designation offer, review the anniversary and renewal dates displayed in Partner Center. To continue your benefits (Azure credits, cloud services, or software), complete renewal during the open 30-day renewal window. If you can't renew within that window, review the qualification requirements for a new purchase after the renewal period.
If you would like to renew during the renewal window, you need to qualify during the qualification eligibility window. For more information, see qualification eligibility window.

Current qualification and renewal availability are different. Review Solutions Partner renewal requirements and check qualification and renewal status separately before interpreting Not applicable or a disabled renewal button as a score problem.
### Partners who meet Solutions Partner designations qualification requirement
New or existing partners can buy or renew their Solutions Partner designation membership. You should make the payment and then enjoy the benefits associated with new Solutions Partner membership.
## Benefits with Solutions Partner designations

To support you as you grow your business, the Solutions Partner designation offer provides a benefits bundle that aligns to the six Solutions Partner designation pathways. The three Azure Solutions Partner designation pathways share core benefits, and each have incremental benefits. For more information, download the MAICPP benefits guide.
## Solutions Partner designations are prerequisite to Specializations

To enroll into a Specialization, you need to already be enrolled into the aligned Solutions Partner designation pathway. See the following section to map specializations to the relevant Solutions Partner designation pathways.
### Benefits associated with Specializations and Azure Expert Managed Services Provider (MSP)

With Solutions Partner designations, specializations, and Azure Expert Managed Services Provider (MSP). When you enroll into a specialization, you receive additional specialization benefits subject to a maximum cap by designation pathway. These additional benefits align with your Solutions Partner designation enrollment anniversary date. For more information, see the MAICPP benefits guide.
Specialization's solution area | Maximum number of Specializations allowed to get benefits

Business Applications | 3
Modern Work | 3
Security | 3
### Map Specializations to relevant Solutions Partner designations
Specialization aligned to solution areas | Solutions Partner designations required as a prerequisite

lines: # Link your Microsoft Learn profile and Skilling Hub account to Partner Center

In this article, you learn how to link your Microsoft Learn profile and your Skilling Hub account to your Partner Center account. By linking these accounts, your organization gets credit for the trainings, certifications, and other learning credentials that you complete in Microsoft Learn, Skilling Hub, and Partner University. You can manage these processes through the Partner Center page for Learn profile linking.
Important

- Partner University was retired on June 15, 2026. Assessments completed prior to this date will remain valid and will continue to count towards skilling scores for Solutions Partner Designations (SPD) and Specializations until June 15, 2027. For more details, see What is happening with Partner University (PU)?

- Partner Center Skilling recently launched profile linking through Skilling** **Hub, enabling learners to connect learning profiles from external platforms such as LevelUp. Since September 28, 2026, learners can link their profiles once through Skilling Hub, allowing eligible learning achievements to flow seamlessly into the Partner Center skilling experience.
Important

Retired certifications: If an eligible certification is earned before its retirement date, the certified individual continues to receive credit for that certification for one year after the certification's retirement date. During this period, the certification continues to be counted toward the applicable skilling requirements for Solutions Partner designations and Specializations.
## What you need to know
Before you start, consider the following information and requirements:

- Microsoft Learn is an online learning platform that helps you gain skills and earn Microsoft verified credentials. It also contributes to your organization's skilling scores for membership programs, such as Specializations and Solutions Partner designations.
- Skilling Hub brings together the credentials that you earn on other Microsoft skilling platforms. You link it in addition to your Microsoft Learn profile:
- What it adds: Certifications, assessments, and trainings from other Microsoft skilling platforms count toward your organization's skilling scores.
- What it doesn't replace: Microsoft Learn credentials don't come through Skilling Hub, so keep your Microsoft Learn profile linked too.
- How to link: See Link your Skilling Hub account to Partner Center.

- You need to have access to Partner Center to link your profiles. Your account admin can create a user for you in Partner Center with your official email ID. You don't need any specific role to link your profiles. The partner account that your user account belongs to must be enrolled in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program.
- You need an active Microsoft Learn profile to link it to Partner Center. To learn more, see Manage your Microsoft Learn Profile settings.

- We recommend that you complete at least one valid Microsoft Learn credential (for example, a certification) on Microsoft Learn before you link your profile to Partner Center. To check your certifications or other credentials on your Microsoft Learn profile page:
- Sign in to Microsoft Learn.
- Select your profile avatar, and then select Profile > Transcript.
- You can link multiple Microsoft Learn profiles to Partner Center by following the flow directed in the next section, similar to linking first Microsoft Learn profile.
- To view your completed Microsoft Learn certifications that count toward Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program offers, select View learnings.
- To view your Skilling Hub certifications, assessments, and trainings that count toward Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program offers, select View learnings.
## Link your Microsoft Learn profile to Partner Center
Follow these steps to link your Microsoft certifications to your Partner Center profile, so that your organization gets scores and is counted in skilling:
- Sign in to Microsoft Learn and complete at least one certification or a valid Microsoft Learn credential.
- Sign in to the Partner Center page for Learn profile linking.
- Select the Microsoft Learn tab under the overview section if it isn't already selected.
- Select Link Microsoft Learn Profile. Follow the process of linking when you're prompted, by using the same account credentials you use to log in into your Microsoft Learn Profile.

After you link your profile, your certifications and assessments appear in Partner Center within 10 days. Your organization also gets qualifying points for specializations or Solutions Partner designation offerings. Please note that newly earned certifications or credentials will also take up to 10 days to appear in your profile.
Before you link or unlink a profile, review the linking and unlinking rules.
## Unlink your Microsoft Learn profile from Partner Center
- Sign in to the Partner Center page for Learn profile linking .
- Select the Microsoft Learn tab under the overview section if it isn't already selected.
- Select Unlink option corresponding to the account in the list of linked accounts Microsoft Learn profile.
When you unlink your profile, it stops your certifications from being credited to your organization. You can link your profile to another Partner Center account if you want.
Note
You can link or unlink your profile up to three times per year. After each link, you must wait 30 days before you can link again. For more information, see Linking and unlinking rules.
## Link your Skilling Hub account to Partner Center

Skilling Hub brings together the certifications, assessments, and trainings that you complete on other platforms. When you link your Skilling Hub account, these credentials count toward your organization's skilling scores if they're relevant. You link Skilling Hub once; you don't need to link each platform separately.
Before you start, consider the following requirements:

- You need to have access to Partner Center to link your account. Your account admin can create a user for you in Partner Center with your official email ID. You don't need any specific role to link your account. Your user account must belong to an organization with an active Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program membership.
- Microsoft Learn credentials don't come through Skilling Hub. Keep your Microsoft Learn profile linked as described in Link your Microsoft Learn profile to Partner Center.
To link your Skilling Hub account:
- Sign in to the Partner Center page for Learn profile linking.
- Select the Skilling Hub tab.
- Select Link Skilling Hub Profile.
- Review the privacy notice, and then select Accept. You can't link your account without accepting the notice. To learn more, see How Partner Center uses your Skilling Hub data.
- Sign in with the account that you use for Skilling Hub.
## Unlink your Skilling Hub account from Partner Center
- Sign in to the Partner Center page for Learn profile linking.
- Select the Skilling Hub tab.
- Select Unlink next to the linked account.
When you unlink your account, your Skilling Hub credentials stop counting toward your organization.
Note
You can link or unlink your Skilling Hub account up to three times per year. After each link, you must wait 30 days before you can link again. For more information, see Linking and unlinking rules.
## Linking and unlinking rules
These rules apply to both your Microsoft Learn profile and your Skilling Hub account.
Important

Frequent linking and unlinking affects how certifications, roles, and benefits eligibility are recognized in Partner Center. Keeping your profiles linked to the same organization prevents delays in validating Solutions Partner qualifications and avoids unnecessary blockers.
- Yearly limit: You can link or unlink your profile from an organization up to three times per year.
- Cooldown period: After you link your profile, you must wait 30 days before you can link it again.
- Changing companies: Every link and unlink counts toward your yearly limit. For both Microsoft Learn and Skilling Hub, linking to a new company automatically unlinks you from the previous one.
These limits help maintain an accurate association of employment and certifications in Partner Center.
## How Partner Center uses your Skilling Hub data
When you link your Skilling Hub account:
- Partner Center shares your Partner Center user account and organization with Skilling Hub, so that your credentials are associated with the right organization.
- Partner Center receives your certifications, assessments, and trainings from Skilling Hub daily.
- Admins in your organization can see your linked credentials.
- Partner Center uses your credentials to calculate your organization's skilling scores for Solutions Partner designations and specializations.
- Partner Center keeps a record of when you link and unlink your account.
## Frequently asked questions
Use these frequently asked questions to learn more about linking profiles in Partner Center.
### What is a Microsoft account?

A Microsoft account is a personal account that's used to access Microsoft services and products, such as Outlook, OneDrive, Xbox, and Microsoft 365. It typically involves an email address and password that you use to sign in across Microsoft platforms for both personal and work-related activities. To learn more, see How to create a new Microsoft account.
### Which Microsoft Learn account should I use for linking — personal or corporate?

Microsoft Learn and Partner Center profile linking supports both personal and corporate accounts. The key consideration is to use the Microsoft Learn account that contains the certifications or credentials you want to link.
### Can a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program admin link the profiles for all users?
No. Each user must sign in to Partner Center and link their own profile. This requirement helps protect your privacy and data.
### What should I do if I have trouble linking my Microsoft Learn profile to Partner Center?

We recommend that you ensure that you complete at least one certification on Microsoft Learn and that you use the same Microsoft account for both platforms. If you still have problems, contact support.
### How do I link my LevelUp profile in Partner Center?

Ensure you have an active Partner Skilling Hub account. If you do not already have one, create a profile and access LevelUp through Partner Skilling Hub. Learners with both LevelUp and Partner Skilling Hub accounts will be automatically redirected to sign in via Partner Skilling Hub.

To have course completions and learning journey badges counted toward specialization or other MAICPP offer requirements, learners must maintain an active Partner Skilling Hub account and use it to authenticate when accessing LevelUp.
### How do I check if I completed at least one certification in my Microsoft Learn profile?

Sign in to Microsoft Learn. Select your profile avatar, and then select Profile from the dropdown menu. On the profile menu, select Transcript. Your transcript displays all successfully completed certifications.
### How long does it take for my certifications to appear in Partner Center?
It usually takes around 10 days for your new credentials or credentials from a new linkage to be reflected in Partner Center specializations or Solutions Partner designation programs.
### How can I link my Microsoft account with a new company?

If you change your company, you can link your Microsoft account with the new company's Partner Center account. Linking to a new company automatically unlinks your Microsoft account from the previous company's account.
### How do I get a list of users who linked their profiles in my organization?
Only the person with the role of Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner admin can download this report. To download the report, use these steps:
- Sign in to Partner Center.
- Select the Settings (gear) icon on the upper right, and then select Account settings.
- Select User management.
- Select the Export learning users link.
A spreadsheet is downloaded with a list of users who linked from your organization.
### How do I get a list of trainings or certifications that users in my organization completed?
Only the person with the role Executive Report Viewer or MAICPP Admin | Report Viewer can download this report
- Sign in to Partner Center.
- On the Partner Center dashboard, select the Insights workspace.
- On the left pane, select Downloads Hub.
- Select Create new report.
- Select Select Membership program.
- Select Basic.
- In the list, select Trainings. Then select the columns that you want and the time range for the report.
- Enter a report name, and then select Download now.
A spreadsheet is downloaded with a list of users who completed various training and certification programs.
Note

This report is available under the Insights hub in Partner Center. To view this report, you should be assigned the role of Report viewer or Executive report viewer. Some sections of this report are only visible to users who are Executive Report Viewers or MAICPP admins. For more information about access control for the Insights reports, see PCI roles.
### What should I do if I reach the limit of associations per year?

You can associate your Microsoft account with a Partner Center account up to three times per year, with a 30-day waiting period between each association. Check your profile for the date when you can start a new association.
### What are the possible reasons for a failure to link a Microsoft Learn profile to Partner Center?
There are two main reasons for a failure:
- Before you link your Microsoft Learn profile to your Partner Center account, you must first complete at least one exam or certification in your Microsoft Learn profile.

- Linking involves multiple systems across the Microsoft ecosystem working together. Occasionally, there might be temporary connection problems, which typically resolve themselves within a few minutes or hours. In such cases, we recommend trying again later.
### Do I still need to link my Microsoft Learn profile if I link my Skilling Hub account?
Yes. Microsoft Learn certifications don't come through Skilling Hub. Link both so that all your credentials count toward your organization.
### Why doesn't a Skilling Hub credential appear in Partner Center?

Partner Center syncs Skilling Hub credentials daily, so new credentials appear after the next sync. If a credential still doesn't appear, make sure that you linked the Skilling Hub account that holds it. If you still have problems, contact support.
### What is happening with Partner University (PU)?
Partner University (PU) was retired on June 15, 2026. This change affects partners who want to enroll in Solutions Partner designations and their specializations. Here's what partners need to know:
- Existing PU user linkings continue to be honored. Partners receive credit and skilling score for these linkings until June 2027.
- After June 2027, all PU assessments will be fully retired and will no longer be used for reporting, skilling score calculation, or as a program requirement.
- No new user linkings to PU are allowed after June 15, 2026.
- The current PU user experience available through the Learn profile page in Membership will also be retired as part of this change.

- Since April 2026, PU assessments are complemented by a new set of skilling requirements. These new requirements are added as an OR condition alongside the existing PU assessments during the transition period.
